title: The Dark Beach
teaser: The witness saw everything, clear as day. That's the problem.

booklet.briefing:
The gift shop at Saltmarsh Bay lifeboat station raises money for the rescue boat. Its collection box is a big model lifeboat full of coins and notes.

At 7:31 pm on the 2nd of December the shop's burglar alarm went off. The window facing the beach had been smashed and the model lifeboat was gone.

A local man, Gideon Pell, phoned the police a few minutes later. He said he'd seen the burglar climbing out of the window and knew exactly who it was.

It looks like an open-and-shut case. Mr. Foxy isn't so sure.
rules: The window was smashed at 7:31 pm, when the alarm went off. The alarm is a siren only; it has no lights or cameras.

suspects.name: Gideon Pell
suspects.description: Retired. Walks his spaniel on the beach every evening. Lost the vote for chair of the lifeboat fundraising committee to Marnie Toll in October.
suspects.motive: Bitter about losing the committee vote to Marnie.
suspects.statement: I was on the sand with my dog, fifty metres from the shop. I didn't need a torch. I saw Marnie Toll climb out of that window, clear as day. I saw her face and that red scarf she always wears.

suspects.name: Marnie Toll
suspects.description: Runs the gift shop. Famous for her red scarf.
suspects.motive: Gideon says she has money troubles. Nobody else has heard of any.
suspects.statement: That's absurd. I was at the pub quiz at The Anchor from seven until gone nine. Half the village was there.

suspects.name: Fergus Dunn
suspects.description: Has a key to the shop and knows the alarm code.
suspects.motive: Could get in at any time.
suspects.statement: I was out on the boat. Tuesday night is crew training.

evidence.title: Scene examination
evidence.body:
Glass from the window lies inside the shop: it was broken from the beach side.

One shard has a smear of fresh blood on it. Blood type: O negative.

Blood types on file (blood donor register): Gideon Pell O negative. Marnie Toll A positive. Fergus Dunn B positive.

When interviewed, Gideon had a fresh cut on his right palm, bandaged. He said he'd cut it opening a tin of dog food.

questions.prompt: Could anyone standing 50 metres away on the beach, with no torch, see a face at 7:30 pm on 2nd December?

options.text: No. It had been dark for almost three hours, there was no moon, thick cloud, and the beach lamps were off

questions.explanation: Last light was 4:41 pm, the moon was new, cloud hid the stars and the council had switched the beach lamps off. The alarm has no lights. It was pitch black.
hints: It's December. What time does it get dark?
Check the almanac for last light, the moon, and then the council notice about the lamps.
Dark since 4:41, no moon, thick cloud, no lamps, no torch. How would you see anyone's face?

questions.prompt: So whose statement cannot be true?
questions.explanation: Gideon claims he saw Marnie's face and scarf clearly with no torch. In that darkness it's impossible.
hints: Somebody described something they couldn't have seen.
Reread the witness statement. What does he claim he saw, and how?
“I didn't need a torch.” On that beach, that night, he'd have needed one badly.

options.text: At the pub quiz in The Anchor

questions.explanation: She handed in round 2 at 7:24 and round 3 at 7:37 in her own handwriting, and the quizmaster saw her by the fire all night.
hints: Marnie says she was at the quiz. Is there a record?
Look at the times the answer sheets were handed in around 7:31.
7:24 and 7:37, both in her handwriting, and she was arguing with the quizmaster.

questions.prompt: Why can't Fergus be the burglar?

options.text: He has a key, so he'd never break a window
He was two miles out at sea on a training exercise
He's lifeboat crew, so he must be honest

questions.explanation: Having a key is suggestive but not proof. The coastguard log is proof: the boat was two miles offshore with Fergus aboard at 7:30.
hints: Having a key makes Fergus less likely to break a window, but that isn't proof. Find proof.
Tuesday night is crew training. Is there a log?
Two miles offshore at 7:30. Not even Fergus swims that fast.

questions.prompt: Who smashed the window and took the collection box?
questions.explanation: Gideon invented a sighting that was impossible in the dark, to frame his rival. The blood on the glass is his type and he has a fresh cut on his palm.
hints: Why would someone invent a sighting?
Look at the blood on the glass and the blood donor register.
A fresh cut, the right blood type and a grudge. The witness is the burglar.

solution.explanation: Gideon Pell smashed the gift shop window in the dark, cut his hand on the glass and grabbed the model lifeboat. Then he called the police to 'report' that he'd seen his rival Marnie do it. He forgot one thing: on a moonless, cloudy December night with the beach lamps switched off, nobody can see a face fifty metres away without a torch.

chain.step: At 7:30 pm on 2nd December it was completely dark: no daylight, no moon, thick cloud and no lamps.
So Gideon's 'clear as day' sighting is impossible. He made it up.
Marnie was at the quiz, handing in sheets at 7:24 and 7:37. Fergus was two miles out at sea.
The blood on the glass is O negative, Gideon's type, and he has a fresh cut on his palm.

eliminations.name: Marnie Toll
eliminations.why: At The Anchor quiz from 7:00, with sheets in her handwriting at 7:24 and 7:37 and the quizmaster as a witness.

eliminations.name: Fergus Dunn
eliminations.why: On the lifeboat two miles offshore from 7:00 to 8:15 pm, logged by the coastguard.
